brief: US equity futures and gold rebound sharply (Nasdaq futures +2.9-3%, SPX e-minis +2%, gold +2.4-2.5%) after last week's selloff, while Asian equities stay net negative (Kospi -3%, having recovered from -5%) despite stabilization measures that lifted Taiex into the green. Citi's equity desk watches SPX e-minis for a close above 7016, then 7149, but stays wary and not an active dip buyer because positioning-driven moves are unpredictable. It expects elevated headline risk around the AI infrastructure cycle and keeps recommending a beta-neutral long strong-balance-sheet, short weak-balance-sheet stock basket. US Rates Strategy argues concerns about the AI selloff will likely restrain the Fed from hiking too quickly, so it holds 5y outperformance with a neutral duration stance pending stabilization. Gold, after its biggest weekly decline in 8 months, is called a medium to long-term buy at $3,000-3,300/oz. Oil is flat: Trump said Iran talks could run into year-end, but Iran's Saturday strike on a Bahrain facility keeps the situation fragile. If Kospi falls further, Citi estimates Korea's NPS pension fund could buy KRW17-62trn of equities at three lower levels, and authorities could also ease buyback caps. IDR rallied on reports MSCI is seeking alternatives to a standalone downgrade.
